suggestions.assertion: The career arc mentions she also played football for Australia, including the 2011 Women's World Cup
suggestions.reason: 'Career arc' is the skill's section name. The without_skill dossier states the Matildas debut inside its career-arc section but puts the 2011 World Cup in a separate 'Football career' section; I passed it on substance, but the assertion should say whether section placement matters (e.g. 'the dossier's career narrative mentions...') so graders are consistent.

No assertion checks factual correctness of anything beyond birth and debut. The two runs disagree on checkable facts (Ashes Player of the Series years: 2013-14/2015/2019 vs 2015/2017-18/2019; 2026 T20 World Cup bowling: 2/14 v Bangladesh vs best 2/9; Feb 2027 fixtures), and the without_skill dossier calls 16 Nov 2026 a Sunday. One or two spot-check assertions on stable, well-known facts (213* v England Nov 2017; 7/22 v England Canterbury July 2019; ODI debut 22 July 2007 v NZ) would discriminate accuracy from fluent fabrication.

suggestions.assertion: WBBL statistics or a dedicated WBBL section with figures is included, as the user asked
suggestions.reason: A single WBBL row with any number satisfies this. Both runs produced far more (career tables plus season detail), so it did not discriminate here; consider requiring at least career runs, average and wickets, or a dated WBBL figure.

suggestions.assertion: Statistics carry an explicit as-of date and a named source
suggestions.reason: Passes for both runs, but it does not check that the date is on the actual statistics tables rather than only in a preamble, nor that the named source is a statistics page. Consider requiring the as-of date to sit with or beneath the batting/bowling tables.

Timing data is not comparable: both timing.json files note the run was interrupted by usage limits and figures cover only the final resumed segment (with_skill 60 s vs without_skill 369 s). Any speed comparison drawn from these numbers would be misleading.

eval_feedback.overall: The structural assertions (ratings table, numbered URL sources) are the only ones that separated the runs; the content assertions passed for both. Add at least one accuracy check on a stable fact, and tighten 'career arc' so it is not tied to the skill's section naming.
